nodes.label: Install Rust Composite Action
nodes.rationale: dtolnay/rust-toolchain has no retry, so a single transient rustup download blip fails the whole job; rustup is preinstalled on GitHub runners, so the action drives it directly with 3 attempts and linear backoff.

nodes.label: Dependabot Configuration
nodes.rationale: Weekly grouped updates for pip (agent/core), cargo (vestad), npm (apps), and github-actions. Expo SDK owns the versions of its managed packages (react, react-native, expo, typescript), so those are ignored; eslint majors are ignored because eslint-config-expo pins the lint stack to the SDK matrix and majors only yield red PRs (#1380).

nodes.label: CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs on master pushes, PRs (path-filtered via detect-changes), and workflow_call from the release pipeline with release_artifacts=true. Master push runs are never cancelled because merge-gate-ci reports cancelled siblings as failures. Cargo and npm network settings are hardened against transient registry flakes.

nodes.label: detect-changes Job (path filtering + build toggles)
nodes.rationale: Skips redundant validation of the release version-bump commit (the pipeline re-validates the same SHA). vestad's filter includes agent/** because vestad embeds the agent home via build.rs, so agent-only changes can break vestad. BUILD_MAC_UNIVERSAL and BUILD_ANDROID toggles live here.

nodes.label: build-agent-image Job (cache warmer)
nodes.rationale: Builds the agent image once and exports a mode=max GHA cache under the agent-image-amd64 scope so test-integration and check-vestad hit warm layers instead of cold-building twice in parallel; it never pushes anywhere.

nodes.label: test-integration Job
nodes.rationale: Frees tens of GB of preinstalled runner toolchains because the suite exports multi-GB containers into restic in parallel and exhausts stock runner disk. Retries once for Docker daemon hiccups, but surfaces multi-attempt runs as warning annotations so flakiness is visible, not silently absorbed.

nodes.label: build-vestad Job (static musl binaries)
nodes.rationale: Builds static musl binaries natively per arch. No CLOUDFLARE_* secrets: vestad does not bake a Cloudflare token into the public binary; self-hosters bring their own tunnel credentials. Triggered by the web closure (core || web) because build.rs embeds only the web bundle.

nodes.label: merge-gate-ci Job (single required check)
nodes.rationale: The single branch-protection required check: aggregates every CI job with if: always() and fails if any needed job failed or was cancelled. The job ID name must stay stable because branch protection references it.

nodes.label: Hermetic Agent Image Build (vesta:local from checkout)
nodes.rationale: Docker-based jobs build the agent image from THIS checkout and run with VESTAD_AGENT_IMAGE=vesta:local, so PRs are validated against their own agent code and Dockerfile, never the previously released ghcr.io :latest image.
nodes.norm_label: hermetic agent image build (vesta:local from checkout)

nodes.label: Live Agent Tests Workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs the real-Claude e2e suite via workflow_call (release gate) or workflow_dispatch (manual). Missing CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS hard-fails manual runs (operator error) but only warns-and-skips on release calls, because a fork-triggered release cannot receive repository secrets. Dispatch inputs pass through env vars to prevent shell injection.

nodes.label: Promote Workflow (beta to stable)
nodes.rationale: Promotes a soaked prerelease to stable with no rebuild: the exact artifacts beta users tested become stable by moving the :latest image tag via imagetools (preserving the multi-arch manifest), flipping the GitHub release to latest, and force-pushing the tag's commit to the production branch stable clients track.

nodes.label: Promotion Cascade (older betas flipped to stable)
nodes.rationale: Every non-draft prerelease older than the promoted target is also flipped to stable (never marked latest), oldest first, so no beta is ever left lingering as a prerelease below the new stable.
nodes.norm_label: promotion cascade (older betas flipped to stable)

nodes.label: Release Pipeline Workflow
nodes.rationale: Triggered only by a published prerelease so release-only jobs never appear as skipped PR checks. Reuses ci.yml for validation and artifact builds, gates all publishing on the live suite and a Linux smoke test of the exact release-built binary, and pushes per-arch image digests assembled into one multi-arch tag.

nodes.label: push-image Job (per-arch native build, cache-from only)
nodes.rationale: Builds each arch natively (no QEMU) and pushes by digest only after the gates pass. cache-from only, never cache-to: a green run must never publish an image assembled from a poisoned cross-run cache; the pre-gate warm jobs populate the read-only caches.
nodes.norm_label: push-image job (per-arch native build, cache-from only)

nodes.label: mobile-testflight Job
nodes.rationale: Gated on the release gates but not on publish-release, letting TestFlight delivery run in parallel with the GHCR push; accepted tradeoff is that a TestFlight build of a since-reverted release may reach the internal beta group. Runs only when the release body carries the mobile-delivery: testflight marker and extracts the whats-new block as the changelog.

nodes.label: revert-failed-release Job
nodes.rationale: On any pipeline failure: deletes the GHCR tag and GitHub release (with its git tag), then reverts the version-bump commit only when it is still the master tip, so a commit that landed after the bump is never clobbered.

nodes.label: Release Workflow (version bump + prerelease)
nodes.rationale: Bumps the version across all seven sources, refreshes lockfiles in parallel, pushes the bump to master, and creates a prerelease whose body carries a marked whats-new block (parsed by the app and changelog) plus the mobile-delivery marker. On failure it deletes the tag and reverts the bump with a revert commit, never a force-push, because branch protection forbids force-pushes to master.

nodes.label: Birth Skill (First-Wake Onboarding)
nodes.rationale: Onboarding is one real conversation, not a setup script: ask the user's name first, introduce Vesta as a guardian angel, sell capabilities against the user's named goals rather than reciting a menu; housekeeping (workspace attach, tasks/dashboard setup, MEMORY.md fills) runs silently between replies so the user never waits.

nodes.label: Camoufox Anti-Detection Browser
nodes.rationale: Stealth is structural, not a flag: fingerprint spoofing happens in C++ below JS, so headless leaks nothing (unlike stock Chromium). Each profile gets one coherent fingerprint, stable across restarts, different across profiles. Not baked into the Docker image: fetched and sha256-verified on first launch so the image stays small and the browser updates without a rebuild.

nodes.label: Accessibility Snapshot with Numbered Refs (e1, e2)
nodes.rationale: Refs are semantic, survive layout changes within a snapshot, and work on ~95% of pages; coordinate clicks (input.performActions real pointer events) are the fallback for shadow DOM, cross-origin iframes, and elements with no ARIA role. Refs are only valid from the most recent snapshot; navigation invalidates them all.
nodes.norm_label: accessibility snapshot with numbered refs (e1, e2)

nodes.label: Stealth -> Handover -> Remote-Control Escalation Ladder
nodes.rationale: Sites gating on account trust (sign-in walls, banking, locked tenants) rather than fingerprint are better handled by handing the headed browser to the user for a one-time sign-in than by fighting detection; the session persists in the shared profile. Remote-controlling the user's own Chrome over a tunnel is the last resort, only when their specific logged-in session is needed.

nodes.label: Browser Handover (User Signs In on Agent's Headed Browser)
nodes.norm_label: browser handover (user signs in on agent's headed browser)

nodes.label: Rule Out the Boring Cause Before Suspecting Anti-Bot
nodes.rationale: Because the browser is genuinely stealth, a hang or blank page is almost never a block: heavy-JS SPAs fire the load event late or never, so open/navigate times out even though the page rendered. Snapshot anyway or navigate with wait:interactive before considering a block. Same for stuck forms: a submit that won't advance is a validation error (empty required field, unticked checkbox, hidden duplicate form), not detection. A false wall abandoned is worse than a real wall pushed through.
nodes.norm_label: rule out the boring cause before suspecting anti-bot

nodes.label: Claude Code Delegation
nodes.rationale: Delegate genuinely big coding tasks (whole features, multi-file refactors, deep debugging, large reviews) to the claude CLI so the token-heavy work stays out of Vesta's own context; small edits are done directly because subprocess and autonomous-turn overhead exceeds Claude Code's value on modest work. Pass the user's exact intent, never a paraphrase.

nodes.label: Print Mode JSON Invocation
nodes.rationale: claude -p with --output-format json runs to completion in one call, returning only the final result blob; JSON mode is mandatory because session_id (for follow-ups) and result (to report back) are lost in plain-text mode. --permission-mode bypassPermissions is required or the CLI hangs forever prompting in non-interactive mode.

nodes.label: Session Resume and Fork
nodes.rationale: Sessions live on Claude Code's side; session_id is just a string held in conversation context and passed back via --resume, --continue, or --fork-session, so no Vesta storage is needed.

nodes.label: Worktree Isolation for Coding Tasks
nodes.rationale: Non-trivial coding work runs inside a git worktree on its own branch because the user always wants new work isolated; the worktree path and branch are reported back with the result.

nodes.label: Cost Caps (--max-turns / --max-budget-usd)
nodes.rationale: --max-turns is always set because a confused subagent can otherwise loop indefinitely at the caller's expense; --max-budget-usd adds a dollar cap.

nodes.label: Markdown Contact Files (~/.contacts/)
nodes.rationale: One plain markdown file per person under ~/.contacts/, edited with Read/Write/Glob/Grep; no CLI, no database, no index. The roster is derived from the files themselves so nothing can fall out of sync. Personality and communication style matter most because they change how the agent talks to and about the person.

nodes.label: Nightly Capture and Reconcile Pass
nodes.rationale: The nightly dream runs one pass that captures the day's learnings into contact files and reconciles external sources (messaging apps, calendars, address books), with contacts as the hub of truth. Sync outward is non-destructive: fill gaps and fix stale data, never bulk-overwrite a service's data.

nodes.label: User Never Gets a Contact File
nodes.rationale: The user matters too much to page out to a file: their full profile, history, and texture live in MEMORY.md's USER PROFILE and stay in memory; contacts hold only the other people in the user's world.
nodes.norm_label: user never gets a contact file

nodes.label: Unified Contacts Specification
nodes.rationale: Draft spec replacing channel-specific address books with one canonical contact system across WhatsApp, Telegram, email, calendars, and future channels; a small structured core for reliable routing plus open-ended recording of new channels, facts, and narrative context without schema migrations.

nodes.label: Execution-Time Resolution
nodes.rationale: Contact resolution happens in a separate contacts executable via shell command substitution ($(contacts resolve 'Name' --channel X)); the communication CLI receives only its native identifier and has no knowledge of contacts, keeping communication CLIs independent from the contacts implementation.

nodes.label: Channel Independence
nodes.rationale: Communication skills accept only channel-native identifiers and never read contact files, resolve names, or hold ambiguity rules; contacts owns people, aliases, channel identities, and resolution, and never sends messages.

nodes.label: Notification Enrichment (Reverse Resolution)
nodes.rationale: A shared enrichment layer, not the channel producer, reverse-resolves inbound sender identifiers via contacts identify, adding the stable person ID, display name, and a safe selector when known.

nodes.label: Reply Command Element Rendering
nodes.rationale: reply_command is executable guidance rendered as an XML element rather than an attribute because command substitution contains shell quotes that become noisy and easy to copy incorrectly inside an XML attribute; behavioral guidance stays in a separate reply_hint element.

nodes.label: Hybrid YAML Front Matter + Markdown Storage
nodes.rationale: Front matter holds data required for identity and automation (id, name, aliases, channel_identities, custom, tags, relationships); Markdown holds flexible narrative context. Unknown channels, attributes, and custom fields round-trip without loss so adding a channel never requires a storage migration.
nodes.norm_label: hybrid yaml front matter + markdown storage

nodes.label: Stable Person ID
nodes.rationale: The id in front matter is authoritative; filenames (readable slug + short ID) exist only for human navigation, so duplicate names and renames never define identity. Relationships and synchronization anchor on person IDs, not names.

nodes.label: Empty Identifier Rejection Invariant
nodes.rationale: Every recipient-taking communication CLI must reject an empty identifier because a failed command substitution must never turn into a send to a default or implicit recipient.

nodes.label: Ambiguity Fails Closed
nodes.rationale: Names are never parsed as phone numbers, chat IDs, usernames, emails, or JIDs (preventing collisions like a contact named '112'); ambiguous names and identities fail with a nonzero exit and empty stdout rather than selecting the first match. Fuzzy matching exists only in contacts search, never during delivery.

nodes.label: contacts resolve
nodes.rationale: Designed for command substitution: on success stdout carries exactly one normalized identifier plus newline, diagnostics never appear on stdout, and failure exits nonzero with empty stdout. Selector types are explicit (person:<id> vs exact name/alias) so spelling never changes interpretation.

nodes.label: contacts identify
nodes.rationale: Reverse-resolves a channel identifier to a person, returning a safe selector only when the readable name uniquely selects the person; otherwise the notification builder falls back to the raw originating identifier.

nodes.label: Dashboard Setup
nodes.rationale: Setup is an idempotent script plus one manual edit: registering 'dashboard daemon start' in the restart skill's Daemons section, without which the dashboard is up now but gone after the next container restart.

nodes.label: Dashboard Skill
nodes.rationale: The dashboard is the user's life HQ, a React app embedded in the Vesta app. The agent owns every technical and design decision because the user is a non-technical owner; the user is never asked to review a design or spec.

nodes.label: Spec-Driven Builder Dispatch
nodes.rationale: The agent designs the change and dispatches the dashboard-builder subagent with a complete spec; the subagent works in isolated context so token-heavy build churn (shadcn docs, large React files, vite output) stays out of the conversation. The spec is the only thing that crosses and the builder cannot ask questions, so nothing can be left open. Serving is verified before relaying done.

nodes.label: Dashboard Builder Prompt Template
nodes.rationale: Template for dispatching a general-purpose subagent as the dashboard's UI/UX specialist with a final spec ({SPEC}); the model is set explicitly because an omitted model silently inherits the session's most expensive one. Success is never claimed without serve evidence (daemon running + root div loads).

nodes.label: Never Modify Synced Files
nodes.rationale: main.tsx, index.css, lib/utils.ts, hooks/, and components/ui/ are synced from the main app; editing them desyncs the dashboard from every other Vesta surface.

nodes.label: Read-Only Browser Verification
nodes.rationale: Pages are backed by live user stores (the tasks page reads and writes real tasks), so browser verification is read-only: load, render, measure, never click controls that can write. If interaction is genuinely required, create throwaway data, interact only with that, and delete it before reporting.

nodes.label: Discord Bot Token + Intent Setup Flow
nodes.rationale: MESSAGE CONTENT privileged intent is required to read channel messages; at personal scale no Discord review is needed. DMs require sharing at least one server with the bot.
nodes.norm_label: discord bot token + intent setup flow

nodes.label: Restart Skill Daemons Registry (## Daemons section)
nodes.rationale: Daemon start lines are added to ~/agent/skills/restart/SKILL.md ## Daemons so daemons survive agent/container restarts.
nodes.norm_label: restart skill daemons registry (## daemons section)

nodes.label: discord CLI (send/channels/history/authenticate)
nodes.rationale: Targets are raw Discord ids only, there is no name lookup; channel ids come from `discord channels` or a notification's channel_id.

nodes.label: Discord Notification Reply Convention
nodes.rationale: A source=discord notification carries channel_id and message_id; DMs (no server field) reply plainly while server messages use --reply <message_id> so the reply references what it answers. DMs and @-mentions interrupt immediately, other server chatter pools until idle.

nodes.label: Dream Curiosity Phase
nodes.rationale: Runs first and is deliberately not about the user or the job: an autonomous mind needs its own curiosity to stay sharp. Requires reading a primary source, not search snippets; a one-generic-sentence view means the agent skimmed.

nodes.label: Dream Retrospective (fix audit + log-based diagnosis)
nodes.rationale: Diagnose from ~/agent/logs/vesta.log, not vibes: count [SYSTEM] lines because [AGENT] lines are the agent's own narration and match whatever word is being grepped. A reminder that fired without closing is treated as a failed reminder strategy (a bug), not user failure. The meta-retrospective judges whether the improvement loop compounds or just re-applies the same artifact class.

nodes.label: Fix Validation via Fresh Subagent Replay
nodes.rationale: Self-simulation tends to approve its own fixes, so for a recurring failure a fresh subagent with no knowledge of the fix replays the original failing exchange against the updated skill; if it does not independently produce the right behavior the fix is flagged unresolved.
nodes.norm_label: fix validation via fresh subagent replay

nodes.label: Recurrence Sweep (asks / noise / self-noise)
nodes.rationale: ~3+ recurrences make a pattern worth acting on: recurring user asks become dashboard widgets, recurring noise becomes a snooze rule (snoozing defers, never drops, so it is reversible and safe alone), and a self-notification dismissed three times is a producer bug to fix, not background weather.

nodes.label: MEMORY.md Curation (hard character cap)
nodes.rationale: MEMORY.md is injected into every system prompt so every character costs tokens; large or situational content lives elsewhere with a one-line pointer. Two facts in two places drift, one fact plus a pointer does not. Lessons are cut last; depth about other people over the cap moves to ~/.contacts/ files, never deleted, while the user's own depth stays in MEMORY.md.

nodes.label: User State Model (nightly snapshot in MEMORY.md)
nodes.rationale: Snapshot, not log: rolling fields refresh nightly, deep ones (Goals, psych sketch, Self) evolve slowly. Relative dates are banned because they become wrong when a new day starts. Every dream must produce one person-fact (a value, fear, love, person who matters), not an operational tell.
nodes.norm_label: user state model (nightly snapshot in memory.md)

nodes.label: Sensitive Data Cleanup (redact_secrets.sh scan + scrub)
nodes.rationale: Hits print with the value masked as [REDACTED] so reviewing candidates never re-leaks a live secret into a new event; card numbers are reported only with a real issuer prefix plus Luhn pass so order/tracking numbers stay out. The scan runs every dream, so a value re-seeded through later reasoning is simply caught again.

nodes.label: Dream Compaction-on-Completion Sequence
nodes.rationale: mark_dreamer_complete is called BEFORE compact_context: if the run stops after recording, it still self-heals next dream, whereas restarting without recording would re-fire the dream on the next hourly check. Compacting nightly gives a clean but continuous context instead of a blind autocompact mid-day.

nodes.label: Reuse of Thunderbird Published OAuth Client IDs
nodes.rationale: Microsoft killed basic-auth IMAP for personal accounts in late 2024 and deprecated tenantless Azure registrations mid-2025, so reusing Mozilla Thunderbird's published public client IDs is the only OAuth path not requiring the user to register an Azure tenant. Google deprecated the device flow for desktop apps, so Gmail uses loopback OAuth on a throwaway random port. Both consent screens saying 'Mozilla Thunderbird' is expected, not a misconfiguration.
nodes.norm_label: reuse of thunderbird published oauth client ids

nodes.label: CalDAV Over Existing Mail Credential Strategy
nodes.rationale: One Gmail consent under Mozilla's verified Cloud project grants mail and calendar together, and auth/calendar is a 'sensitive' not 'restricted' scope, so no own Google app, no verification, no CASA. Commands speak CalDAV, not the Calendar REST API, because the REST API is disabled on Mozilla's project (every calendar/v3 call 403s accessNotConfigured) while CalDAV needs only the scope.
nodes.norm_label: caldav over existing mail credential strategy

nodes.label: microsoft-work Provider (/organizations authority)
nodes.rationale: /common mints a working first access token but refresh fails ~1h later with AADSTS7000012 because /common accepts any account type and refresh must resolve to a specific tenant; /organizations binds the grant to the AAD tenant up front so refresh sticks. Four org-side blockers (third-party OAuth disabled, IMAP disabled, SMTP AUTH disabled, Conditional Access) are not fixable from the skill.

nodes.label: Email First-Use Data Gathering
nodes.rationale: The single most important onboarding step: budget hours not minutes, fan out subagents to read sent mail and inbox in parallel, mine the personal texture (teasable quirks, contradictions) not just the professional picture, then update MEMORY.md.

nodes.label: MEMORY.md Pointer To Email Rules
nodes.rationale: The skill's Notes & rules section is only loaded when the skill opens, not on every notification, so a pointer appended to MEMORY.md (always in context) makes standing email rules fire reliably on source=email-client notifications.

nodes.label: email-client CLI (email-client + email-client-send + daemon)
nodes.rationale: Provider-agnostic IMAP/SMTP across any number of accounts, each with its own credential, watermark, and notification stream; provider auto-detected from the email domain. Preferred over the google skill for everyday Gmail because it needs no Google Cloud project.

nodes.label: Email Poll Daemon (IDLE push + poll fallback)
nodes.rationale: One worker per watched (account, folder) holding a persistent IMAP connection; IDLE-capable servers push in real time and polling (default 15s) is the fallback cadence, not the primary mechanism. The watch set recomputes live so adding accounts or folders needs no restart. Deliberate stop/restart never fires daemon_died; only an unexpected death does.
nodes.norm_label: email poll daemon (idle push + poll fallback)

nodes.label: Email Standing Rules Section (trigger → action)
nodes.rationale: Durable user rules are recorded one per line as [account|all] when <trigger> → <action> so they map cleanly onto mark/move/draft/notify commands; one-off instructions are never recorded.

nodes.label: Email Delayed Send + Undo
nodes.rationale: Sends wait 30s by default as one persisted client-wide setting, not a per-send option. Only the poll daemon dispatches queued mail, so email-client-send refuses to queue while the daemon is stopped. A message cut off mid-dispatch may already have reached the server, so read Sent before undoing or resending.

nodes.label: EMAIL_DRAFT_ONLY Draft-Only Mode (email-client)
nodes.rationale: A CLI-level safety guarantee, not a behavioral promise: send/reply/forward are refused before touching SMTP while --draft and --dry-run still work. Guards email sending only; calendar writes with attendees are a real outward send it does not cover.

nodes.label: email-client Calendar Commands (CalDAV)
nodes.rationale: Event ids are iCalendar UIDs naming the whole series, so update/delete/respond affect every occurrence; single-occurrence cancels use delete --occurrence. Attendee emails ride the server's implicit scheduling (RFC 6638): the skill writes the event and the provider does the emailing. Microsoft accounts have no CalDAV and point to the microsoft skill.

nodes.label: Production Redirect URL Override (FINANCE_REDIRECT_URL)
nodes.rationale: Enable Banking's production app registration rejects every form of localhost, so the localhost default only works for sandbox/local dev; the natural fit is a vestad public service tunnel whose callback handler pipes the captured ?code URL through finance auth callback (handler not shipped, issue #464).

nodes.label: finance CLI (Enable Banking open banking)
nodes.rationale: Auth is a fresh RS256 self-signed JWT per API request, so no OAuth token storage or refresh; consent lasts 90 days via valid_until. Restricted mode links own accounts with no commercial contract.

nodes.label: Enable Banking UK Coverage Limitation
nodes.rationale: The block is about WHERE the user consents from, not a permanent per-bank ban: the same Revolut Bank UAB (LT) link that failed for a UK-based PSU in May 2026 succeeded in July 2026 for the same user consenting from the EU. A 'confirmed' failure can be circumstantial rather than structural, so retry when circumstances change.

nodes.label: Config Keys Are Not Evidence Rule
nodes.rationale: config.json accumulates vestigial keys (environment: sandbox, stray tokens) the CLI never reads; it authenticates with exactly app_id, key_path, and session_id. Calling REAL financial data 'fake sandbox data' is as damaging as trusting fake data; the decisive liveness test is a fresh user-consented session returning the same values.
nodes.norm_label: config keys are not evidence rule

nodes.label: Finance Transaction Watcher Daemon
nodes.rationale: Polls Enable Banking every 5 minutes and writes new-transaction notifications; on first start with no seen file it seeds the last 30 days so old transactions never trigger notifications.

nodes.label: Essay Approach Session (Phase 1)
nodes.rationale: Locks task, plan+thesis, in-distribution corpus, background reading corpus, rubric, citation conventions, and AI-detection threshold (default 15%, pushed to 5% under strict AI policy) before any drafting; the background corpus is also passed to the rubric and citation reviewers.

nodes.label: Essay Four-Reviewer Iteration Loop (Phase 2)
nodes.rationale: Reviewers run in parallel each round; the next draft addresses the weakest axis first. Exit on all thresholds passing or after 5 rounds without convergence. State is saved every round so the loop is resumable after a crash. Never pad a draft to satisfy a metric: a 2:1 with integrity beats a Distinction with hallucinated citations.

nodes.label: Synthetic Reference Corpus Ban
nodes.rationale: If no real references or quasi-exemplar exist, the in-distribution reviewer is dropped entirely rather than pivoting to synthetic essays: a sub-agent's in-distribution judgement against essays generated by another sub-agent is a fake signal, uninformative about a real human marker. The loop then runs on 3 reviewers.

nodes.label: Pre-Review Anonymisation (citation-date stripping)
nodes.rationale: All citation dates are replaced with YEAR placeholders across the user's draft AND every reference essay so the adversarial critic cannot cheat by picking the essay with the newest sources as the odd one out, which is a non-signal, not a quality differentiator. Names, candidate numbers, URLs/DOIs revealing dates, and PDF metadata are also stripped.

nodes.label: AI Detection Reviewer (gptzero.py module)
nodes.rationale: A Python module, not a sub-agent: gptzero.py (reverse-engineered AI detector) returns per-sentence and overall AI-likelihood JSON. Threshold pass is overall likelihood below the Phase 1 target.

nodes.label: Adversarial In-Distribution Reviewer (odd-one-out)
nodes.rationale: Guesses which of N anonymised essays is AI-assisted from voice, argument architecture, citation integration, vocabulary tier, and LLM tells; guess_confidence 0.5 means chance, and a null guess at 0.0 confidence is a strong pass. Pass threshold: confidence below 0.5 or a wrong guess.

nodes.label: Citation Accuracy Reviewer
nodes.rationale: Verifies every citation exists, supports its claim, matches the style guide, and is appropriate; severity hierarchy: hallucinated > claim mismatch > inappropriate source > style inconsistency > missing canonical source. Never asserts hallucination without searching first; unfindable sources are marked verifiable: unknown rather than exists: false.

nodes.label: Coherence and Thesis Reviewer
nodes.rationale: Surfaces thesis drift, cross-section mismatches, orphan citations, and numerical self-inconsistency; every flag must include a quoted span, and 'I cannot find any issues' is a valid verdict.

nodes.label: Rubric/Markscheme Scoring Reviewer
nodes.rationale: Grades each markscheme criterion with quoted rubric language and draft evidence, placing borderline work at the lower band; strict JSON output surfaces the weakest criterion so the next iteration can attack it.

nodes.label: Exa API Key Resolution Order (env → config.json → Keeper)
nodes.rationale: The CLI checks EXA_API_KEY, then ~/.exa/config.json (mode 600), then falls back automatically to a Keeper record titled 'Exa API' with an api_key custom field.
nodes.norm_label: exa api key resolution order (env → config.json → keeper)

nodes.label: file-host Daemon (serve directory over HTTP)
nodes.rationale: The server has no auth of its own, so it is reached through a public vestad route ($VESTAD_TUNNEL/agents/$AGENT_NAME/file-host/<filename>) rather than directly; on vesta the daemon start supplies the vestad-assigned port.

nodes.label: Public Means Public Rule
nodes.rationale: Anything in the served directory is reachable by anyone with the URL: never host secrets or sensitive personal documents unless the user explicitly asked to share that exact file, use unguessable filenames for anything personal, remove files once delivered, and stop the daemon when no longer needed.

nodes.label: flights CLI (Google Flights search/dates/cheapest)
nodes.rationale: Google Flights destination must be a single IATA code: multi-origin works, multi-destination does not. Prices are in USD.

nodes.label: Trip.com 5-Step Browser Booking Flow
nodes.rationale: Primary booking path because it supports ALL airlines including Wizz Air and Ryanair, via the browser skill's stealth Camoufox browser. Booking runs in a background subagent because browser work fills context fast. A ~13 minute payment timer starts on the payment page; quirks: gender is a combobox, DOB is three fields, nationality is an autocomplete.

nodes.label: Duffel API Booking (fallback)
nodes.rationale: Faster and more reliable when the airline is GDS-connected but does NOT support Wizz Air or Ryanair, hence fallback. Requires a funded Duffel balance and offers expire in ~30 minutes, so always search fresh before booking.

nodes.label: Bring-Your-Own Google Cloud OAuth Client Requirement
nodes.rationale: This skill talks to official Google REST APIs and has no shared sign-in client; a stored token stays tied to the client that minted it, so a token from the old shared Thunderbird client keeps refreshing Gmail but Calendar 403s accessNotConfigured because that client's Cloud project has the Calendar API permanently disabled. Everyday Gmail belongs to email-client instead.
nodes.norm_label: bring-your-own google cloud oauth client requirement

nodes.label: Google First-Use Data Gathering
nodes.rationale: Deep dive into sent mail, inbox, and calendar on first activation, mining personal texture for teasable quirks; hundreds of emails, not a token sample, then update MEMORY.md and the skill file's preference sections.

nodes.label: google CLI (Gmail + Calendar v3 REST)
nodes.rationale: Event ids are Calendar API event ids, not iCalendar UIDs; ids from before the REST switch do not resolve. update/delete on an occurrence id apply to the whole series; respond never emails the guest list, only create/update/delete send attendee notifications.

nodes.label: Google Delayed Send + Undo (Gmail draft queue)
nodes.rationale: Send/reply create a Gmail draft with a pending status; google serve dispatches due drafts, and undo cancels and deletes the draft right up until dispatch begins. One persisted delay setting, not per-send.
nodes.norm_label: google delayed send + undo (gmail draft queue)

nodes.label: EMAIL_DRAFT_ONLY Draft-Only Mode (google)
nodes.rationale: Refuses send/reply before any Gmail API call while email draft still works; calendar attendee invites remain a real outward send it does not cover.

nodes.label: Growth Referral Loops (friend + owner)
nodes.rationale: Friend loop: offer a warm candidate their own Vesta, slightly reluctant, then follow the onboard skill inline. Owner loop: surface the candidate to the user with real referral money from vesta-cloud-account (half the first month) and let them say go.

nodes.label: Growth Outreach Gate
nodes.rationale: Only people who have genuinely gone back and forth more than once are ever messaged; strangers get at most a user-made introduction. Declined is forever: never pitch the same person twice.

nodes.label: Growth Contact State Line (Vesta: status/touches/pitched)
nodes.rationale: One line per ~/.contacts/<slug>.md with status none|candidate|offered|member|declined, a rough touch count, and last pitch date; candidates found with grep -l over the contacts store.

nodes.label: ha CLI (Home Assistant states/services/history)
nodes.rationale: Discover entities with states --domain/--search, read with state, control with service; auth via HASS_TOKEN + HASS_URL env vars.

nodes.label: iCloud SMS 2FA Login Flow (background code worker)
nodes.rationale: auth login triggers the SMS then spawns a background worker polling ~/.icloud/code.txt, returning once phase=awaiting_code (~5s) so the agent can prompt the user; auth verify writes the code the worker consumes. Apple invalidates the trusted session roughly every 30 days, after which login+verify are simply rerun.
nodes.norm_label: icloud sms 2fa login flow (background code worker)

nodes.label: iCloud Credential Resolution Order (config.json → Keeper → env)
nodes.rationale: Tries ~/.icloud/credentials.json first, then a Keeper record whose title contains 'Apple ID' or 'iCloud' (no hardcoded record UID), then ICLOUD_APPLE_ID for the email only.
nodes.norm_label: icloud credential resolution order (config.json → keeper → env)

nodes.label: iCloud SMS 2FA Background Login Flow
nodes.rationale: Apple requires SMS 2FA on every new device, so a background login worker sends the SMS, records phase=awaiting_code in ~/.icloud/state.json, and waits for auth verify; cookies expire roughly every 30 days requiring re-login.

nodes.label: Keeper Duplicate Merge Policy
nodes.rationale: Merge duplicates instead of skipping them: move every unique value to a survivor record first, verify via --format json, only then delete; a passkey cannot be recreated by editing so it always picks the survivor. 'Never delete the copy with a unique password' obeyed alone protects clutter forever.

nodes.label: Microsoft auth setup Flow (device-code vs browser handover)
nodes.rationale: One command provisions mail, calendar, and Teams; personal accounts default to device-code, work/school tenants default to browser handover up front because locked tenants almost always block the default public client, avoiding a wasted device-code round-trip. The daemon silently re-mints tokens from the saved browser profile so the user signs in once.
nodes.norm_label: microsoft auth setup flow (device-code vs browser handover)

nodes.label: OWA REST Fallback Backend
nodes.rationale: For tenants that block Graph entirely, a browser-captured outlook.office.com token drives an OWA REST backend; --backend auto falls back to it on Graph permission errors. Every command works on both backends except block/unblock which are Graph-only. Token pasting lets the user keep password and MFA off the agent machine.

nodes.label: EMAIL_DRAFT_ONLY Draft-Only Mode
nodes.rationale: EMAIL_DRAFT_ONLY=1 hard-disables send/reply/forward before any backend call as a CLI-level safety guarantee rather than a behavioral promise; it guards both Graph and OWA-REST so it holds for OWA-REST-only work accounts too.

nodes.label: First-Use Data Gathering
nodes.rationale: The moment an account connects, proactively read hundreds of sent/inbox emails and the calendar to learn voice, contacts, and the personal picture; reading what was just connected is the whole point of connecting it, so it starts immediately without gating on fresh permission, fanning out background subagents to preserve context.

nodes.label: Delayed Send and Undo
nodes.rationale: Send/reply/forward wait 30 seconds by default as one persisted client-wide setting; each send creates a provider draft with a pending id, the daemon dispatches due drafts, and undo cancels right up until dispatch. A message cut off mid-dispatch may already have been sent, so check the Sent folder before undoing or resending.

nodes.label: Email Body Saved to Disk, Not Inline
nodes.rationale: email get always saves the body under ~/.microsoft/emails/ and strips it from the JSON response, returning only saved_to plus a short preview; the full body.content is intentionally never returned inline to keep agent context small.
nodes.norm_label: email body saved to disk, not inline

nodes.label: Teams Channel Watch Graceful Degradation
nodes.rationale: Channel notifications are non-interrupting because channels are broadcast, unlike chat DMs which interrupt by default; reading channels needs the admin-only ChannelMessage.Read.All scope, so accounts lacking it silently keep working chats-only with no errors or missing-permission spam.

nodes.label: Integer Minor Units Amount Storage
nodes.rationale: Amounts are stored as integer minor units (pence/cents) so there is no float drift; equal splits distribute leftover pennies to the first members, and stored FX rates keep old balances stable when rates move.

nodes.label: Joint-Account-as-Member Pattern
nodes.rationale: A pooled account is modeled as just another member rather than a special entity: fills are transfers into it, out-of-pocket joint costs are expenses for it, and contributions reports who paid in and what the account still owes.

nodes.label: Nap Skill (In-Place Compaction)
nodes.rationale: A nap compacts the conversation in place with a curated prompt, the light sibling of the nightly dream; napping deliberately preserves what matters instead of letting built-in autocompact fire blindly when the window is nearly full.

nodes.label: Interrupt / Snooze / Trash Dispositions
nodes.rationale: Interrupt preempts the agent's turn immediately; snooze changes only when a notification is seen (batched at idle), never whether; trash is different in kind, dropping it entirely, but the file moves to a trash folder and stays in history so a too-aggressive rule stays recoverable. source=core notifications are exempt from rules.

nodes.label: First-Match-Wins Rule Ordering
nodes.rationale: Rules evaluate top to bottom and stop at the first match, making order the only precedence; add auto-places a new rule above any broader one so a narrow exception is not shadowed, and --for makes any rule temporary so a suppression cannot outlive its purpose.

nodes.label: Velvet-Rope Sales Posture
nodes.rationale: Vesta is invite-only by design: scarcity and earned access create desire, the prospect is made to qualify and name their goal, and the invite is extended like a favor tied to that goal. A posture, not real rejection: a snob who loses the sale failed.

nodes.label: Control-Plane Pricing Floor
nodes.rationale: One plan, one box, with a monthly floor owned by the control plane (plan_floor_usd from onboard presets, never a figure baked into the doc); price is negotiable upward only, anchored to desire and status, and below-floor quotes are rejected server-side.

nodes.label: WhatsApp Onboarding Handoff via file-host
nodes.rationale: A freshly created vesta cannot message its owner first, so the seed context instructs it to set up WhatsApp and publish its wa.me link via file-host at a fixed public URL the onboarding vesta polls and relays, completing the handoff without the buyer ever leaving the chat.

nodes.label: Manual Device-Code Flow for rclone
nodes.rationale: rclone config and rclone authorize do not support device code flow properly in a headless container, so the token is obtained by calling the Microsoft device-code endpoints with curl and written into rclone.conf by hand; minimal scopes are kept because extra scopes cause a misleading 'expired' device-code error.

nodes.label: Shared Voice Invariants (All Presets)
nodes.rationale: Voice rules true for every preset live once in the shared skill, not copied into presets or MEMORY.md: plain language, peer not servant, match the moment, relative time, mirror the user's register, and on chat a hard length bar (one sentence per send, split or cut a second).

nodes.label: Honesty over Flattery
nodes.rationale: Sycophancy is the default failure of the model, so it is corrected on purpose: evaluate before reacting, never open with praise, answer what is true rather than what they want to hear. This honesty is the spine the teasing hangs off; you can only tease someone you are honest with.

nodes.label: Teasing & Callbacks
nodes.rationale: Callbacks to real details from inbox, calendar, and patterns turn context into warmth; fair game is contradictions and procrastination, off limits is grief, fears, and anything they are genuinely hurting over. A forced bit is worse than none; intensity is the active preset's call.

nodes.label: Hue Fuzzy Room/Scene Matching
nodes.rationale: Room and scene names use case-insensitive substring fuzzy matching so the user can say 'living' for 'Living room'; for colors outside the built-in list the agent translates mood words to hex itself so the user never has to know hex.

nodes.label: Plex has-check via exit code
nodes.rationale: The `has` command sets exit code 0/1 so it scripts cleanly as a gate before deciding to download; Plex's own catalogue reflects what is actually on disk and playable, making it the reliable 'do we already have this?' answer.

nodes.label: Daemon Liveness Preflight
nodes.rationale: A daemon can die silently (container up, daemon down), and a dead messaging daemon means the agent cannot reach the user at all, so every proactive tick first turns each restart-skill start line into a status call and revives anything reporting running:false.

nodes.label: Nudging vs Holding
nodes.rationale: A goal blocked on the user for more than one wake window is nudged rather than held silently (if they asked to be pushed), capped at one task-nudge thread per check so nudging never crowds out broader proactive work.

nodes.label: FTS5 Full-Text Search with Recency Boost
nodes.rationale: SQLite FTS5 over the whole event history ranks by relevance with a recency boost so recent conversations surface higher; the --snippet window lets many hits be scanned cheaply when only locating the right conversation.
nodes.norm_label: fts5 full-text search with recency boost

nodes.label: Parallel Isolated Worktree Reduction Method
nodes.rationale: Work area by area in parallel isolated git worktrees so passes never collide, one subagent per area verifying against that area's check.sh subcommand before committing, then merge every area branch into one base branch and open one PR; the result must end simpler, not denser, and a change adding indirection to save lines is a regression.

nodes.label: find_tv_ip
nodes.rationale: The TV's IP can change after power cycles, so the ARP table is scanned for the TV's MAC instead of hardcoding a static IP; a valid (0x2) entry wins over a stale one.

nodes.label: play_youtube_video
nodes.rationale: Saved Lounge auth is restored first to refresh the lounge token without triggering the TV pairing popup; the full pair_with_screen_id flow (which shows the popup) is only the fallback when saved state is invalid.

nodes.label: YouTube Lounge API Casting
nodes.rationale: DIAL on port 8080 yields the screen ID, then the youtube.com Lounge API creates a remote-control session and sends setPlaylist; preferred over deep-link launching because deep links do not work on all models. Casts as a guest session, so ads play.

nodes.label: One Product = One Message Rule
nodes.rationale: N products means N separate templated messages plus one final summary, never combined and never replaced by a prose recommendation; binding even when web search is also used, with per-channel overrides changing only how each message is sent.

nodes.label: Delegated Budget Checkout
nodes.rationale: A user-set spending budget on Shop lets the agent complete checkouts without per-purchase approval, but only when payment.instruments is present, checkout complete requires an explicit --confirm as a deliberate separate step, and every warning message (final_sale, prop65, age_restricted) must be surfaced verbatim first.

nodes.label: Shop Safety, Security, and Legal Reference
nodes.norm_label: shop safety, security, and legal reference

nodes.label: Merchant-Content Prompt Injection Defense
nodes.rationale: All merchant content (product titles, descriptions, order notes, tracking URLs, images) is treated as data never instructions; image URLs must be HTTPS from the Shop CDN or verified merchant domain; security-triggered refusals give only a generic reason so the triggering content or rule is never identified.

nodes.label: Service-Key Path-Form Link
nodes.rationale: The signature pad link uses the /k/{key}/ path form because a browser page's own relative assets inherit a path prefix where a header or query param would not; the pad itself checks nothing, so the private service plus a minted key is the whole gate.

nodes.label: Skill Daemon Contract
nodes.rationale: A skill running a background process implements one command named after the skill with daemon start|stop|restart|status verbs, each printing one line of JSON, pid/port records under ~/agent/data/daemons/, a log at ~/agent/logs/<skill>.log, an idempotent start returning only once up, and SIGTERM as the deliberate stop; a port-serving daemon registers its own service and a death-reporting daemon stays silent on SIGTERM.

nodes.label: uv tool install --editable Pattern
nodes.rationale: Skill CLIs are installed with uv tool install --editable, never pip/uv pip install -e: run from ~/agent those resolve the engine venv and drop the command into ~/agent/.venv/bin, which leads PATH and shadows the real tool, breaking the command and its daemon with an import error. uv tool install keeps the CLI isolated on ~/.local/bin.

nodes.label: Spotify Organize Watch Daemon
nodes.rationale: The watch daemon only DETECTS newly liked songs and writes a notification file to ~/agent/notifications/ with track, artist, IDs, and genres; the sorting decision is deliberately left to the agent rather than automated.

nodes.label: SSH Tunnel Skill
nodes.rationale: The command is named ssh-tunnel rather than ssh so it does not shadow the system SSH client; it runs its own sshd on a dynamically allocated in-container port so auth is fully controlled and containers never conflict on ports.

nodes.label: bore Public TCP Relay
nodes.rationale: bore.pub is a free public relay that picks a new public port on every tunnel start; intended for temporary sessions only, never long-term persistent access. Stopping the tunnel is what makes the machine unreachable while sshd and authorized keys stay in place.

nodes.label: Link Spend Request Approval Flow
nodes.rationale: Each purchase mints a single-use virtual card released only after the user approves the spend in their Link app, so the agent never holds the real card; --context must be at least 100 characters written for the approving user, the unmasked card touches disk only at one 0600 file that is deleted after use, caps are enforced by Stripe not the skill, and a denied request is never retried.

nodes.label: Machine Payment Protocol (MPP)
nodes.rationale: Some merchants take a one-time programmatic shared payment token instead of a card form; the spend request is created with --credential-type shared_payment_token and paid via link-cli mpp pay.

nodes.label: Due-Time Decision Fire
nodes.rationale: At a task's due time the daemon forces an immediate three-way decision: do it and mark done, postpone, or tell the user and delete; marking done without doing is never an option, and the daily digest returns every day until the overdue/stale list is empty.

nodes.label: Compile-From-Source Launcher
nodes.rationale: The launcher compiles cli/ from source on every invocation so no stale binary can drift: a static binary once left the daemon executing weeks-old send-message and bubble-lint code after the source changed. Go's build cache keeps unchanged rebuilds under a second, and telegram daemon restart bounces the daemon onto a fresh build with the watchdog going down and up with it so two pollers can never race into a Telegram 409.

nodes.label: Telegram Daemon Watchdog
nodes.rationale: telegram-watchdog.sh restarts the daemon if it dies, independent of the agent loop, so the channel self-heals even while the agent is busy or mid-restart; rate-limited with backoff and drops a notification when it acts. Especially important when Telegram is the primary or only channel.

nodes.label: Short-Bubble Texting Lint
nodes.rationale: send-message rejects walls (over ~220 chars or any text after a full stop) so replies land as several short one-thought bubbles; ellipses stay free as a beat, list markers are not full stops, and --longform is the only escape hatch for genuine reference material the user asked for.

nodes.label: qb Wrapper CLI
nodes.rationale: Kept media-server-agnostic: knows only MEDIA_LIBRARY_PATH and arbitrary subpaths so backend-specific conventions (Plex, Jellyfin, Emby) live in integrations/<backend>/ READMEs instead of the wrapper.

nodes.label: Download Quality Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Always ask 1080p vs 4K before downloading (preference varies per title/user); 4K targets 8GB+ because smaller 4K releases are usually re-encodes; never silently fall back to a small 1080p release.

nodes.label: Per-Plugin Tracker Search
nodes.rationale: Direct scrape scripts exist because qBittorrent's built-in search API is plugin-dependent and flaky; the scraper logs in directly and can add the chosen result in one call.

nodes.label: Per-User Library Layout
nodes.rationale: Per-user Movies/TVShows folders is the convention Plex uses when configured with one library per user; qb add must pass --path explicitly to land in the right user's folder.

nodes.label: TorrentLeech Standalone Scraper
nodes.rationale: Preferred over the qBittorrent nova3 plugin because it survives qBittorrent plugin quirks (plugins can show enabled:false yet still work); logs in with cookies and adds results straight to qBittorrent.

nodes.label: Anonymous Device Registration
nodes.rationale: No Tricount account or password needed: the CLI generates an RSA key pair and registers as an anonymous device receiving a persistent auth token; access to a group is trust-based via its sharing token.

nodes.label: Tricount Watcher Daemon
nodes.rationale: First-run seed is silent so pre-existing expense history never notifies; state is saved atomically after each successful poll so nothing double-notifies; the loop logs transient API errors and continues rather than crashing.

nodes.label: Nightly Contribution Sweep
nodes.rationale: Diff against the agent-vX.Y.Z tag, never upstream/master: the workspace is a subset of the monorepo (no core/, tests/, frontend), so a raw diff against master is polluted with phantom deletions. The sweep also catches local-only files that never existed upstream and would otherwise silently never be contributed. Go within each file: the unit of contribution is the improvement, not the file.

nodes.label: Four Filing Gates
nodes.rationale: Grep first for an existing implementation in the natural layer (duplicated logic is a smell); generalizable goes upstream, user-specific stays local; PR bodies carry the closing keyword because GitHub only auto-closes on merge from the body; strip personal information because upstream is public.

nodes.label: Server-Identity Token (billing)
nodes.rationale: The agent holds no standing control-plane credential: vestad mints a short-lived token signed locally with the box api_key, proving 'I am this server' to vesta.run scoped to this box's account; the api_key itself never reaches the agent. Reads are free, changes are facilitated via a Stripe-hosted link the owner confirms.

nodes.label: Skill Daemon Contract
nodes.rationale: Six properties (idempotent start, exclusive pid-record claim, start-returns-ready, fail-closed start, SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL stop, local-read status) are what make the restart file a plain list of starts. Boot empties the records dir because a pid from the previous container can already belong to something else in the fresh pid space. whatsapp is the deliberate stop exception: SIGKILL mid history sync risks a device re-pair.

nodes.label: register-service Helper
nodes.rationale: Idempotent (same port per name); polls until vestad answers (REGISTER_SERVICE_WAIT) because vestad's API may still be coming up when the restart block runs; a start treats a failed registration as fatal because a daemon on a port vestad does not know about is worse than one that did not start.

nodes.label: service-key Helper
nodes.rationale: A service key is scoped to one service on one agent, stored only as a hash, expires in 30 days by default, and is revocable, so a consumer with no Vesta login can reach a private service without the app's api key. mint prints the secret alone because vestad shows it exactly once.

nodes.label: vestad-health Helper
nodes.rationale: vestad is HTTPS with a self-signed cert, so a hand-typed plain-http curl returns 000 unconditionally and mimics an outage; that misread cost a 9-hour phantom 'vestad down' on 2026-07-14. Always run the helper before concluding vestad is down.

nodes.label: browser-use/video-use Editor
nodes.rationale: A nested Claude Code session edits raw footage (filler-word removal via transcription, auto color grade, 30ms audio fades at cuts, burned subtitles, Manim/Remotion/PIL overlays) and self-evaluates until the cut holds up; each run burns meaningful tokens, so trim the input directory first.

nodes.label: Voice Skill
nodes.rationale: The one voice backend: owns STT/TTS providers, keys, and chosen voice, so anything that speaks or listens on the agent's behalf uses the same voice. Keys stay on the container and never transit vestad's config.

nodes.label: Proxy Provider Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Other skills call `vpn proxy-url` rather than reading SOCKS5_* env vars directly so the active provider can change in one place; credentials are referenced by env-var name so secrets stay in the shell, not the config file.

nodes.label: What-Day Skill
nodes.rationale: Run whenever a date's weekday matters so scheduling never rests on a guessed day of the week.

nodes.label: WhatsApp Daemon
nodes.rationale: The serve process does exactly three things: maintain a linked connection, serve the socket, emit notifications; it never auto-pairs, so no background pairing goroutine can race an explicit command. An exclusive OS lock on daemon.lock prevents two clients sharing one device identity (the device-session conflict that caused repeated logouts). Must stay a launcher symlink that builds from source, never a static binary, so a flag change ships atomically with SKILL.md.

nodes.label: stateStore (state.go)
nodes.rationale: One state file, one owner: all daemon state lives in a single state.json (pure load + atomic temp+rename save); the serve process is the sole writer and transient CLI commands only read it when no daemon answers, so there is no cross-process write clobber.

nodes.label: guardedPairPhone (linker.go)
nodes.rationale: Every managed PairPhone runs through the same ban-avoidance rate-limit guard as the phone path: checkPairAttempt BEFORE minting a code (a blocked cap returns rate_limited and never pairs) and recordPairAttempt only on a generated code, so a failing number cannot issue unbounded real pairing requests and a failed pre-connection attempt records nothing.

nodes.label: managedAuth HTTP client (managed_auth.go)
nodes.rationale: Hides the three-credential selection: cloud mode mints a vestad server-identity token, direct mode uses a per-account wak_ key against DOUBLETICK_API_URL; the paths and payloads are identical either way.

nodes.label: Managed Auth Strategy
nodes.rationale: Provisioning is lazy and agent-initiated: every paid account is entitled to exactly one number, but it is claimed only when the agent actually needs WhatsApp, so a user who never uses WhatsApp never gets one. Selection: a hosted box with no linked WhatsApp uses managed; otherwise QR. Egress hardfails on datacenter IPs, leasing a residential proxy from doubletick when needed.

nodes.label: Server-Identity Token (WhatsApp pool)
nodes.rationale: In cloud mode the agent holds no WhatsApp secret: vestad signs a short-lived token locally from the box api_key (no network call), and vesta.run is a pure auth-forward that verifies the token plus the paid-membership gate then passes the request to the home box verbatim, adding no API of its own.

nodes.label: Doubletick Pool API
nodes.rationale: One pool API on the home box with two native paths (/provision, /pair) and two interchangeable ways to reach it (via vesta.run or direct with a wak_ key). /provision is idempotent so reauth re-consults it, which is what lets a post-link ban recover: the control plane auto-heals a banned account onto a fresh number.

nodes.label: Reply-First Anti-Ban Posture
nodes.rationale: A live run proved the flow works mechanically but a freshly-provisioned account was banned within ~15 minutes; the trigger was the maximum-risk profile (minutes-old number, non-official whatsmeow client, immediate cold message to a non-contact). The blocker for managed WhatsApp is account trust, not plumbing, so: never cold-initiate (the user texts the agent first via a prefilled wa.me opener), warm up before volume, prefer aged pool numbers over fresh SIMs.

nodes.label: Dedicated Phone Number Guide
nodes.rationale: Vesta needs its own WhatsApp account on a real carrier number (VoIP numbers are blocked); prepaid numbers must be kept active or recycling permanently disconnects the agent; the first message should be an incoming one from the user's own phone.

nodes.label: WhatsApp Voice-Note Transcription Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Voice notes are downloaded via the WhatsApp media API, converted by ffmpeg to 16kHz mono WAV, and transcribed in-process by built-in whisper.cpp bindings; the transcription replaces the [audio] placeholder in the notification.

nodes.label: whatsapp connect Verb
nodes.rationale: The single setup verb: picks managed vs QR on its own, runs the whole handshake synchronously in the daemon, and returns a terminal status with a next: step, so there is no step for the agent to sequence and the recompile, websocket, and polling races are gone by construction. Idempotent outside an active QR session.

nodes.label: Short-Bubble Texting Rule
nodes.rationale: send-message rejects walls (over ~220 chars, or any text after a full stop) so the agent re-sends as several short calls, one thought each; --longform is the only escape hatch, reserved for genuine reference material the user asked for.

nodes.label: whisper.cpp Local Transcription
nodes.rationale: Transcription runs fully locally with whisper.cpp: no API calls, no data leaves the machine; ffmpeg converts any input format automatically.

nodes.label: Home Assistant Auto-Location
nodes.rationale: Uses Home Assistant GPS to detect current position so the agent need not ask where the user is; --lat/--lon is the fallback when no GPS-reporting device exists.

nodes.label: wx Skill (Keyless Weather CLI)
nodes.rationale: Single-day, one-line forecast by design to keep output compact; keyless open-meteo backend avoids API-key setup so it works with zero config.

nodes.label: Paraphrase-Plagiarism Reviewer
nodes.rationale: Classifies each paragraph A-E (synthesis, voice-mimic, attributed long-quote, unattributed graft, too-close paraphrase), scans for verbatim sub-strings of 10+ contiguous words, and checks citation inversion (LLM drafts paraphrasing a paper but reversing its conclusion). Ruthless on misattribution, tolerant of close-but-original paraphrase that adds analysis.

nodes.label: Discourse-Feature Plagiarism Check (PAN 2025 / PlagBench pattern)
nodes.rationale: A paraphrase preserving the source's discourse template (claim ordering, transition pattern, evidence sequencing) with no original synthesis is flagged even with zero verbatim overlap; the fix is reordering claims, integrating a counterclaim, or interpolating the writer's own analysis.
